pages.text: Life's first molecules polymerise (Arrhenius, Eₐ = 60 kJ/mol) while water hydrolyses them (80 kJ/mol). Copying is imperfect: Eigen's error threshold says a genome of length L survives only if L < ln σ / µ. Sparks drive chemistry but also mutate.
$(thing)Set$(): Reactor temperature, Monomer concentration, Spark & UV flux.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Temperature swings: the error rate varies by ±10%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): Error catastrophe: the genome cannot persist; The crucible cannot be held colder than its coolant.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Synthesis rate follows the yield and the energy supply.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Polymerisation rate: k = A·e^(−Eₐ/RT)$(br)Hydrolysis rate: k_h = A_h·e^(−E_h/RT)$(br)Polymer yield: Y = k_p c/(k_p c + k_h)$(br)Copy error µ: µ$(br)Error threshold: L_max = ln σ / µ
